messages:
maya (AE): Quick note from the NovaHealth POC run earlier today. We drove a steady 120 rps for 20m with intermittent 60s spikes up to 600 rps (3 spikes). Baseline p50/p95 looked fine but p99 during spikes jumped from ~210ms to ~1.1s. Can infra/ML take a look? Need a short troubleshooting list for the follow-up call. :eyes:

ryan (SRE): Thanks. Two quick asks: paste the load generator invocation and the exact model + runtime config. Also confirm whether pods scaled down between spikes or stayed warm.

maya (AE): Loaders: we used vegeta from a k8s job: `echo "POST https://api.redwood.prod/v1/generate" | vegeta attack -rate=120 -duration=20m -header "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -body=payload.json > results.bin`. For spikes we launched a second vegeta attack at rate=600 for 60s. Model: `redwood/steady-7b` with quant profile `q5_0`. Replicas started at 4, autoscaled to 10 during bursts. No explicit warmup before the test.

lucas (ML Eng): Likely contributors: kernel JIT/priming and KV cache invalidation on prefix churn. With `q5_0` you can still see kernel variance on big seq length changes. Two experiments: 1) steady low-rate hammer (20 rps) for 10m to keep kernels/kv populated, 2) run a short primer of common prefixes just before spikes. Also, capture `runtime_events.log` with `--trace-events` on the harness.

jen (Solutions): On sizing: for sustained 120 rps with `redwood/steady-7b` our guidance is 1 x A40-equivalent per ~80-100 rps depending on tokens per request. For that test I'd recommend baseline 2 GPUs with autoscale to 6 for bursts. Estimated committed spend range (region-dependent): $18k-$30k/mo. Include a 10% buffer for burst reserve in contract.

ryan (SRE): Practical checklist for the run: 1) pin traffic to a single AZ (avoid cross-AZ autoscale), 2) set min_replicas >= 2 so pods don't drop to zero, 3) increase `pod_grace_period` so scaling doesn't evict warm pods, 4) disable cross-region fallback in routing.

maya (AE): Good list. Can you also confirm what metrics we should attach to the follow-up? Customer wants a one-page summary.

ryan (SRE): Attach: pod GPU% utilization timeline, request queue length, p50/p95/p99 latency CSV, and `autoscaler_events.log`. If you can include `kernel_compile_count` events from runtime tracing that's helpful.

lucas (ML Eng): If p99 correlates with `kernel_compile` spikes, try `kernel_priming=true` in runtime config or switch quant to `q4_1` for less variance (cost tradeoff). Also examine batch size distribution during bursts — micro-batching can swell latencies if requests arrive in big clumps.

bench-bot: Stress run summary uploaded: results.bin, summary.csv, basic-metrics.json (2242206401).

maya (AE): Attached CSV shows p50 95ms / p95 240ms / p99 1.12s during the spike window. GPU avg utilization jumped from 62% to 98% during spike and then dropped to 22% between spikes.

ryan (SRE): That pattern (high peak utilisation + low idle) indicates pods are cooling between spikes. Two immediate fixes: add small steady background traffic (20 rps) between spikes or set `min_replicas` to 3 and enable `burst_reserve: true` at 15%.

lucas (ML Eng): For the next run, also run the harness with `--latency-samples=20000` and include `trace_events=true`. I'll grep for `kv_miss|kernel_compile|batching_delay` once files are up.

jen (Solutions): On the pricing front, propose a 30-day pilot with a soft commit: baseline 2 GPUs + 2x burst cap for validation, then convert to a 3-node commit if they hit steady-state. That reduces upfront spend ask and addresses their procurement concerns.

maya (AE): Thanks — Ill present the pilot plan. Re-running now with steady 20 rps between spikes and `kernel_priming=true`. Will upload new logs by EOD.

lucas (ML Eng): Great. If new run still shows p99 blips, we can experiment with `quant_profile=q4_1` and re-run a short 10m stress to compare tail variance.

ryan (SRE): One more heads-up: NOVA's security team asked if Dedicated supports customer-managed KMS and audit log retention. Confirmed: yes. I'll DM the SOC doc and flag cust KMS steps.

maya (AE): Perfect. Will circle back after the re-run. Thanks team! :white_check_mark:
